title.narrative: PE Optimization of Lima Water and Sewerage Systems

description.narrative: The objective of the Optimization of Water and Sewerage Systems Project for Peru is to improve efficiency, continuity and reliability of water supply and sanitation services in the northern service area of Lima. There are three components to the project, the first component being rehabilitation of water and sewerage networks in the first northern service area of Lima. This component will finance the rehabilitation of the water and sewerage networks in first northern service area of Lima, directly benefiting more than 158,380 low income people. The exact proportion of replacement and renovation will be determined during implementation based on a detailed hydraulic modeling of each subsector and an agreed methodology. The second component is the Improving Lima's Water and Sewerage Service (SEDAPAL's) efficiency. This component will finance studies and consultant services to provide decision-making tools to SEDAPAL's management to improve the company's efficiency. Finally, the third component is the SEDAPAL project management. This component will finance the additional staff required for project management to establish a monitoring and evaluation system and undertake the required financial audits as well as physical and procurement reviews.
The proposed development objective of this project is to improve efficiency, continuity and reliability of water supply and sanitation services in the Northern Area of Lima.

title.narrative: Number of water utilities that the project is supporting
Number of stakholders (men and women) reached with information on rational water use, including information on water saving equipment

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator is surpassed. The target was revised during the Additional Financing to reflect the expanded scope of the indicator and the introduction of gender disaggregated data to allow monitoring of differentiated impacts. By end of Project, 11,767 stakeholders were reached under Lima Norte I interventions and 230,373 beneficiaries were reached under Lima Norte II activities.</p>
<p>As part of SEDAPAL’s Social Action Plan, this included educational workshops about rational use of water, handwashing andhygiene campaigns, appropriate use of water and sanitation systems, water-saving equipment, notices of water service disruptions, including safety recommendations to the community during civil works, notices for regularization of water/sewerage connections, practical guide for customers to understand customer metering and billing reading, and customer service channels <em>(Central de Atención a Usuarios – CAU)</em> to report incidents or complaints.</p>

title.narrative: Number of stakholders (men and women) reached with information on rational water use, including information on water saving equipment

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement of 64 percent. The target was revised during the Additional Financing to reflect the Project’s scale up. For Lima Norte I, the rehabilitation works were completed in 2015. By end of Project, SEDAPAL had rehabilitated a total of 119.5 km of water supply pipes under Lima Norte I, and 125.8 km under Lima Norte II for a total of 245.3 km. The target was missed because SEDAPAL's carried out emergency rehabilitiation works, thus reducing the number of pipe kilometers to be rehabilitated under the Project.</p>

<p>Achievement rate is 110 percent. The target was revised during the Additional Financing to reflect the Project’s scale up. This indicator is surpassed due to the rehabilitation of 153 km of sewerage pipes under Lima Norte I and 118 km under Lima Norte II for a total of 271 km rehabilitated sewerage pipes.</p>

<p>Target achieved. The target was revised and introduced as an indicator during the Additional Financing to reflect the Project’s scale up. For Lima Norte I, a total of 217,784 people located in districts of Comas, Independencia, San Martin de Porres and Los Olivos were benefitted. For Lima Norte II, a total of 224,508 located in the districts of Comas, Carabayllo, San Martin de Porres, Los Olivos, Puente Piedra, Callao and Ventanilla were benefited, for a total of direct Project beneficiaries of 442,292.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people (men and women) participating in learning events on strategic planning and management

comment.narrative: <p>This target is surpassed. This indicator was revised during the Additional Financing and was moved from PDO level. Between 2015 and 2018, SEDAPAL participated in several workshops and learning events that span a range of topics, including: (waste)water reuse, robust decision-making, drought management, study tour  to Brazil on information technologies for commercial systems, water security, social and environmental compliance, fiduciary management, impact evaluation, among others. By end of Project, a total of 28 men and 25 women from SEDAPAL have attended learning events on strategic planning and management. Unit of measure of indicator should read as "number".</p>

title.narrative: Number of people (men and women) participating in learning events on strategic planning and management
Piped household water connections that are benefiting from rehabilitation works undertaken by the project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate of 93.4. The target was revised during the Additional Financing to reflect the Project’s scale up. By end of Project, 27,460 piped household water connections were rehabilitated in Lima Norte I served districts and 37,418 connections were rehabilitated in Lima Norte II areas. The target was missed because SEDAPAL's carried out emergency rehabilitiation works, thus reducing the number of water connections to be rehabilitated under the Project.</p>

title.narrative: Piped household water connections that are benefiting from rehabilitation works undertaken by the project
Annual incidence of water pipe breakages per km of water supply network in the project area.

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 46.7 percent. The end target was changed during the Additional Financing and the new target was overly ambitious as explained in the Efficacy section. At project closing, Lima Norte I achieved an annual incidence of water pipe breakages of 0.14 and Lima Norte II achieved a value of 0.17</p>

title.narrative: Annual incidence of water pipe breakages per km of water supply network in the project area.
Number of daily hours water services are provided in the project area.
Percentage reduction in Non Revenue Water (% of volume invoiced/volume distributed)

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. This indicator was modified during the Additional Financing to reflect a more appropriate performance indicator to measure operational efficiency. A combination of structural and non-structural measures, particularly to improve the commercialunctions at SEDAPAL, has led to a remarkable reduction of NRW levels in 15 percentage points. In addition, SEDAPAL has committed to the implementation of a NRW reduction plan (see related IRI in Component 3). At Project closing, Lima Norte I had 26 percent of NRW levels; Lima Norte II had 25 percentage of NRW.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage reduction in Non Revenue Water (% of volume invoiced/volume distributed)
Annual incidence of sewerage blockages per km of sewerage network in the project area.

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 84.8 percent. This indicator was revised during the Additional Financing. Annual incidence of sewerage blockages in Lima Norte I was 1.01 and 1.02 in Lima Norte II. This Causes for not achieving the end target are related to inadequate use of the sanitation system, combined with reduced routine operation and maintenance activities in 2020 due to the COVID-19 emergency.</p>

title.narrative: Annual incidence of sewerage blockages per km of sewerage network in the project area.
Evaluation of current and future demand for water and sanitation services completed together with identification of priority actions to meet such demand as efficiently as possible.

comment.narrative: <p>Target not achieved. The water demand and supply assessment study was not possible to be completed during the implementation of Lima Norte I due to failed negotiations with the bidders, hence the consultancy was dropped. However, in 2019, SEDAPAL resumed the initiative and conducted an internal basic supply-demand study as part of the development of the 30-year master plan and, by end of Project, the utility continued to implement an internal communication plan.</p>

title.narrative: Action plan completed for the integration of GIS and SCADA systems.

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. The Project supported several studies that were satisfactorily completed by the end of Project, despite some setbacks during Project implementation. These studies are: (i) GIS digitalization cadaster of WSS networks rehabilitated under Lima Norte I; (ii) new communications platform and integration of Lima and Callao wastewater treatment plants to SEDAPAL’s backbone network; (iii) integration and standardization of the SCADA system; (iv) preparation of Terms of Reference for the implementation of a new commercial and operational incidents system; and (v) design of a telecommunications and automatization center (data center).</p>

title.narrative: Study on options for the development of a new organizational model completed.

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. The assessment for a new organic structure at SEDAPAL was completed by 2019. By end of Project, SEDAPAL’sproposal of a new organization structure, that followed the study’s recommendations, was pending to be approved by the <em>Fondo Nacional Empresarial del Estado</em> (FONAFE).</p>

title.narrative: Evaluation of current and future demand for water and sanitation services completed together with identification of priority actions to meet such demand as efficiently as possible.
Action plan completed for the integration of GIS and SCADA systems.
Study on options for the development of a new organizational model completed.
No. of schools reached with information on rational water use, including information on water saving equipment

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator is surpassed. The target was revised during the Additional Financing to reflect the expanded scope of information and the outreach exercise targeted to schools. By end of Project, SEDAPAL had implemented outreach campaigns in 33 schools in Lima Norte I and 92 schools in Lima Norte II. Educational workshops aimed at schools’ staff, students and parents included topics about rational and safe use of water, adequate use of WSS equipment, among others (see IRI 6 under Component 1).</p>

title.narrative: No. of schools reached with information on rational water use, including information on water saving equipment

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate of 99 percent. The target was introduced as an indicator during the Additional Financing. The Project supportedthe consolidation of SEDAPAL’s grievance redress mechanism and social action plans. Between July and November 2020, SEDAPAL had received 108,990 complaints and resolved 91,896.</p>

title.narrative: Integrated Non-Revenue Water management Action Plan elaborated and approved by SEDAPAL's General Management and Board

comment.narrative: <p>Target not achieved. An integrated NRW plan was not able to be developed during Project implementation of Lima Norte I, yet it did not hinder the attainment of the PDO. SEDAPAL developed an internal NRW plan, which included the following key actions: increased metering, improved commercial management, and targeted pipe replacements. SEDAPAL’s management has been very active and committed implementing several NRW activities configured with Bank support, which have allowed the company to remarkably achieve its NRW targets.</p>
